title: Open the instance once its caches are loaded

blocks.text: Each instance of the pricing service warms its caches at startup, each cache on a thread of its own, and tells the load balancer it is ready only when every loader has finished. A cache that can't be loaded doesn't stop the instance: it starts without that cache and logs which ones are missing.

The gate that holds the startup thread back has failed twice. One instance never reported ready, although its log showed all three caches loaded, the first of them within a few milliseconds. On the day the tax-rules service was down, no instance reported ready at all.

items: `runLoader(...)`: each loader's thread runs its loader through it;
`awaitLoaded(...)`: the startup thread waits there, up to its timeout.

blocks.text: When you're done, the startup thread gets `true` as soon as every loader has finished, however early they finished and whether or not they failed, and `false` if its time runs out first. About eight lines in total; you may add fields.

cases.says: a startup thread that is already waiting is let through once the last of three loaders finishes
with one of three loaders unfinished, the wait ends with false when its time is up
when every loader finished before the startup thread began to wait, the wait answers true at once
a loader that throws still counts as finished, and its cache is listed as failed

origin.section: A Latch or a Queue Remembers a Signal That wait() Can Miss

concepts: A latch remembers only what it is told: a loader that throws before countDown() leaves the waiter waiting until its timeout.
notifyAll() wakes only threads already waiting and records nothing, while a latch keeps its count, so a signal sent before the wait is not lost.
